newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says Germany loser in row with Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Germany loser in row with Tehran.

text.p: Germany is the real loser in its diplomatic row with Iran over a Berlin court verdict implicating the Islamic Republic's leaders in political murders, Tehran's interior minister said.

Iran's official news agency IRNA on Tuesday quoted the minister, Ali Mohammad Besharati, as telling deputies in the northeastern city of Mashhad that the West was wrong to believe Iranians would be "intimidated through threats and pressure".
A Berlin court two weeks ago jailed an Iranian and three Lebanese for the murder of four Kurdish dissidents and accused Tehran of ordering the killings.
Besharati on Monday dismissed allegations by the German judge as "mere political propaganda orchestrated by Zionist brokers and fugitive terrorists from Iran", IRNA said.
The judgment prompted the 15-nation European Union to abandon its "critical dialogue" policy with Iran and -- with the exception of Greece -- recall envoys for consultation.
The verdict prompted an official protest from Iran's leadership and unleashed a wave of protests in Tehran. Thousands of people took to the streets, with some trying to storm the German embassy.
Besharati repeated Iranian assurances Tehran was committed to protecting foreign residents "who can reside in Iran without any worries," IRNA said.
Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and Iran's ambassadors to the EU met in Tehran on Monday and discussed ties with the European bloc, IRNA said.
"They discussed the guidelines of the (spiritual) leader of the Islamic revolution Ayatollah Ali Khamenei regarding the recent developments in Irano-European ties," it said.
"Safeguarding the honour and interests of the Islamic republic and its relationships...and political attitudes of European governments were also discussed," the agency said.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has appealed for calm in European states. In conciliatory remarks on Sunday, he said a "pause for thought" was needed to consider how Germany and the rest of Europe should redefine relations with Tehran.
He said he would discuss the future shape of relations with Iran with his EU counterparts at a meeting on April 29.

The EU's "critical dialogue" had been aimed at keeping lines of communication with Iran open in the face of a U.S. policy of isolating Iran. The EU has been trying to promote pro-Western elements and human rights in the Islamic Republic.
